adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:321 — With Init removed from every RPC, the initErr "service is stopping/stopped" gate set by Stop() is never checked, so Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search keep running against a stopped backend and cancelled watcher instead of failing

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:137 — Narrowing cacheMu to the map write lets concurrent getOrCreateIndex calls for the same key build in parallel, and the last one wins, overwriting (and leaking without Close) an index that handleEvent may already have written events into, so those updates are lost

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held cacheMu for the entire method, but the diff removes that and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx` (lines ~85-137). This allows two goroutines to concurrently build separate Bleve indexes for the same `key` and then race to store into `b.cache`, with the last write winning. Since the overwritten index is not closed here, it can be leaked. More importantly, callers may write to/receive events on one index instance while subsequent lookups use the other cached instance, causing divergence and potential loss of indexed updates depending on how the rest of the system retrieves the index from the cache.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:137 — Narrowing cacheMu lets concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key (Search RPC plus handleEvent via getOrCreateIndex) run in parallel, and the last write to the cache wins, so docs written to the losing index are dropped; no concurrent same-key test runs under -race.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held cacheMu for the entire function, but now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx` at the end. From the diff alone, this means multiple goroutines can execute the full index-build path concurrently and then race to populate the cache, with the last finisher overwriting the cached index. If another goroutine obtained/used the earlier-built index (e.g., to index an event) before it gets overwritten, subsequent readers using the cache will not see those writes, creating a real risk of lost indexed documents. The diff shows no per-key singleflight/guard to prevent same-key concurrent builds.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a log line calling `s.search.TotalDocs()` in `searchSupport.init`, but it does not show `TotalDocs()` implementation or that it "ranges over b.cache" without a lock. adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:304 — Nothing tests the new Init ordering (search index before initWatcher), for example that a search-init failure no longer starts the watcher, or that writes landing during the initial index build end up indexed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes initialization sequencing inside server.Init: it now initializes the search index first (`s.search.init(ctx)`) and only then starts watching (`s.initWatcher()`), whereas previously the watcher started before search init (see reordered block around `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go` ~300). This is nontrivial behavioral logic, and the diff does not add or adjust any tests to assert the new ordering or its consequences (e.g., that a search init failure prevents the watcher from starting, or that events during initial index build are handled as intended). This is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap rather than a proven defect.
